latin.444: §. VIII. Neque tamen adhuc dum canonizata sic Transsubstantiatio, extra omne concussionis & eversionis periculum posita fuit, quin licentiosæ Scholasticarum Disceptationum incudi subjiceretur ab ipsis quoque Scholasticorum Doctorum Antesignanis, genuinum Conversionis modum in omnem partem & quaqua versum disquirendo versantibus.
latin.445: À Johanne Parisiensi, semet illis associante & à pag. 30. & 50. ad 77. Copiosiori numero adductis, opinionibus.
latin.446: Verò eorum ad duodenarium redactis numerum per Werenfelsium nostratetem, Concione de Sacra Coena Germ. p. 30.
latin.447: Quinimo ex Reformatoribus Pontificiæ Idolomaniæ, tàm XIV. quàm XV. Seculo exsurrexerunt, qui partim Ruperti Tuitiensis & Ascelini, de Consubstantiatione, vel Crassiori, vel Subtiliori, partim Veterum pristinæque Ecclesiæ de Supernaturali & Spirituali Corporis Christi in S. Coena præsentia, reducem fecerunt, inque hodiernum usque diem servant, haud morati fulmen brutum expelvi Tridentina.
latin.448: Quô Transsubstantiationi ita cautum legitur Sessione XIII. cap. 4. Can. 2. p. m. 130. initio: Quoniam Christus Redemptor noster, corpus suum, id quod sub specie panis offerebat, verè esse dixit; ideo persuasum semper in Ecclesia Dei fuit, idque nunc hæc sancta synodus declarat, per consecrationem panis & vini Conversionem fieri totius substantiæ panis in substantiam corporis Domini nostri & totius substantiæ vini in substantiam sanguinis ejus, quæ Conversio convenienter & propriè à sancta Catholica (Romana) Ecclesia TRANSSUBSTANTIATIO est appellata.
latin.449: Proinde, si quis dixerit in SSmo. Eucharistiæ Sacramento remanere substantiam panis & vini unà cum corpore & sanguine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, negaveritque mirabilem illam & singularem Conversionem totius substantiæ panis in corpus, & totius substantiæ vini in sanguinem, manentibus duntaxat speciebus panis & vini, quam quidem Conversionem Catholica (Romana) Ecclesia aptissimè Transsubstantiationem appellat, Anathema sit. Nec morati Papæ definitionem, Conciliiq; injustam Confirmationem, ut juxta hanc Transsubstantiationis, non aliam formam, professio & juramentum fidei fiat, utque unus hic è novis Symboli Romani articulis sub tenore & pœna frequenti hujusmodi exaudiatur: Ego N. firma fide credo & profiteor omnia & singula, quæ continentur in symbolo fidei, quo S. Romana Ecclesia utitur; … profiteor pariter in Missa atque in Eucharistiæ Sacramento esse verè realiter & substantialiter corpus & sanguinem unà cum anima & divinitate Domini nostri Jesu Christi, fierique conversionem totius substantiæ panis in corpus & totius substantiæ vini in sanguinem Christi, quam Conversionem Catholica (Romana) Ecclesia Transsubstantiationem appellat: vide Bullam Pii IV. Confirm. Concil. Trident. super forma juramenti professionis fidei unà cum eodem Concilio editam.
latin.450: Nec denique morati articulum insuper hunc, Symboli Romani XIIItium tali Epiphonemate & interminatione Papæ claudi: Nulli ergo omnium hominum liceat hanc paginam nostræ voluntatis & mandati infringere vel ei ausu temerario contraire. Si quis autem hoc attentare præsumpserit, indignationem omnipotentis Dei ac beatorum Petri & Pauli Apostolorum ejus, se noverit incursurum. Datum Romæ ap. S. Petrum, Anno Incarnationis Domini 1564. Idibus Novembris.

pass_a.444: §. VIII. Nor however, even once Transsubstantiation was thus canonized, was it placed beyond every danger of concussion and overthrow — rather it was still subjected to the anvil of licentious Scholastic Disputations by the standard-bearers themselves of the Scholastic Doctors, turning over and searching the genuine Mode of Conversion in every part and every which way.
pass_a.445: Opinions being adduced in a more copious number by John of Paris, associating himself with them, and from pp. 30 and 50 to 77.
pass_a.446: But their number reduced to a dozen by our Werenfels, in the German Concio on the Sacred Supper, p. 30.
pass_a.447: Nay from the Reformers of pontifical Idolomania there arose in both the fourteenth and the fifteenth Century those who partly restored Rupert of Deutz and Ascelinus on Consubstantiation, whether Crasser or Subtler, partly the Ancients’ and the pristine Church’s [teaching] on the Supernatural and Spiritual presence of Christ’s Body in the Holy Supper, and keep it even to this day — not delayed by the brute thunderbolt cast out by Trent.
pass_a.448: By which Transsubstantiation is so guarded as is read in Session XIII chapter 4 Canon 2 p. 130 at the beginning: Since Christ our Redeemer said that what He offered under the species of bread was truly His body; therefore it has always been persuaded in the Church of God, and this holy synod now declares, that by consecration of bread and wine a Conversion is made of the whole substance of bread into the substance of our Lord’s body and of the whole substance of wine into the substance of His blood, which Conversion is conveniently and properly called by the holy Catholic (Roman) Church TRANSUBSTANTIATION.
pass_a.449: Accordingly, if anyone shall say that in the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist the substance of bread and wine remains together with the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and shall deny that marvelous and singular Conversion of the whole substance of bread into body and of the whole substance of wine into blood, the species of bread and wine alone remaining, which Conversion the Catholic (Roman) Church most aptly calls Transsubstantiation — let him be Anathema. Nor did they delay the Pope’s definition and the Council’s unjust Confirmation, that profession and oath of faith be made according to this form of Transsubstantiation and no other, and that this one among the new articles of the Roman Symbol be heard under such tenor and frequent penalty: I N. with firm faith believe and profess all and each contained in the symbol of faith which the Holy Roman Church uses; … I likewise profess that in the Mass and in the Sacrament of the Eucharist there is truly, really and substantially the body and blood together with the soul and divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ, and that a conversion is made of the whole substance of bread into body and of the whole substance of wine into Christ’s blood, which Conversion the Catholic (Roman) Church calls Transsubstantiation — see the Bull of Pius IV confirming the Council of Trent on the form of the oath of profession of faith published together with the same Council.
pass_a.450: Nor finally did they delay this article further, the thirteenth of the Roman Symbol, being closed with such an Epiphonema and threat of the Pope: Therefore let it be lawful for none of all men to infringe this page of our will and mandate or to contradict it by rash daring. But if anyone shall presume to attempt this, let him know he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed Apostles Peter and Paul. Given at Rome at St. Peter’s, in the Year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1564, on the Ides of November.

444: §.VIII: even after canonization, Transsubstantiation is not past concussion or overthrow.
Scholastic standard-bearers still hammer the genuine Conversion-mode on a licentious disputation-anvil — every part, every which way.
445: John of Paris joins those Antesignani.
From his pages 30 and 50–77 a more copious heap of opinions is adduced.
446: Our Werenfels trims that heap to a dozen.
Source: his German Concio on the Sacred Supper, p. 30.
447: Fourteenth- and fifteenth-century reformers of pontifical idolomania also rose.

Some restore Rupert of Deutz and Ascelinus on Consubstantiation (crasser or subtler); others restore the pristine Church’s supernatural and spiritual presence of Christ’s body in the Supper — and keep it to this day, undeterred by Trent’s brute thunderbolt.
448: Trent Sess. XIII cap. 4 Can. 2 (p. 130): because Christ said what He offered under bread-species was truly His body, consecration converts the whole substance of bread into His body and of wine into His blood.
That conversion the holy Catholic (Roman) Church conveniently and properly calls TRANSUBSTANTIATION.
449: Anathema if anyone says bread and wine substance remain with body and blood, or denies that singular conversion with species alone remaining.

Nor do they delay the Pope’s definition and the Council’s unjust confirmation: profession and oath must follow this Transsubstantiation form — Ego N. … truly, really, substantially body and blood; conversion of whole substances — Pius IV’s bull on the Trent faith-oath.
450: That thirteenth Roman-Symbol article closes with Pius IV’s threat: none may infringe this page; presumers incur God’s and Peter and Paul’s indignation.
Dated Rome at St. Peter’s, 13 November 1564 (Ides).
